reason: E1 directly supports that O and N interstitials promote phase segregation and cause softening in a refractory HEA, but it does not address Ti-Ni-based alloys or the specific processing intervention. E2 is about elemental effects in HfMoNbTaTiZr alloys and does not provide evidence on impurity control or its impact on mechanical properties. Thus, only the general mechanism of interstitial-induced segregation and softening is supported, while the applicability to Ti-Ni-based systems and the efficacy of the proposed processing route lack cited evidence.
premises: Interstitial impurities (O, N) promote phase segregation and precipitate formation in refractory high-entropy alloys at elevated temperatures.
Phase segregation and precipitate formation due to interstitials cause softening and loss of ductility.
Reducing interstitial impurities will suppress deleterious secondary phases and maintain a uniform solid solution.
Maintaining a uniform solid solution enhances elevated-temperature strength and ductility via solid solution strengthening.
Ultra-high purity processing can effectively reduce interstitial impurity levels in Ti-Ni-based HEAs.
